label: prop:skein-crossing-asymmetry
title: Crossing asymmetry and per-crossing Coulomb correction
html:
Proposition. Crossing asymmetry and per-crossing Coulomb correction

The Skein relation assigns positive crossings a weight of q and negative crossings a weight of q^{-1}:

  q  L_+ -  q^{-1} L_-
  =  (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}) L_0.

For q > 1, the per-crossing repulsive Coulomb correction relative to a mixed-charge baseline evaluates to:

  \delta_{\mathrm{Coulomb}}
  =  q -  \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1})
  =  \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})
   >  0.

The ratio of the antisymmetric (Coulomb) to symmetric (strong) Skein weights is:

  \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  =  \tanh(\ln q).

At q = 1, the asymmetry vanishes. As q \to \infty, the ratio approaches 1.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. The generic categorical/q-deformation identities it relies upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
